text.p: Bonds opened strongly as the whole of Europe breathed a sigh of relief when the Bundesbank left its repo unchanged at three percent, calming immediate concerns of a German rate rise, traders said.
Nevertheless, European markets could struggle if the dollar continued to rise against the mark as this would rekindle the rate fears, they added.
Traders said the market was waiting for the results of the Institute for Public Credit Management's auction for 25 billion escudos of three-year bonds.
The Bundesbank decision could boost interest at the sale, they added.

A Reuter poll of four banks and one broker, carried out before the Bundesbank announcement, had forecast an average yield of between 5.34 and 5.39 percent against Monday's 5.31 percent close on the secondary market.
